reviews.name: Mohammed Idrees
reviews.text:
I have been visiting Islamic Center of West Georgia for more than 3 years, and I can honestly say this masjid has become a very special place for me and my family.
Imam Saab Dr. Atiq Patel is truly a blessing from Allah for the people of Douglasville. The amount of time, effort, and dedication he gives to the community is something that deserves appreciation. His guidance, lectures, and the way he connects with people make a big difference in the lives of many.
I also want to appreciate brother Nabil, Sultan Habib, and many others who are always working behind the scenes for the masjid. Running a masjid and serving the community is not an easy job, and the effort of these brothers should be recognized.
Over the years, I have seen the love, care, and commitment that goes into making this place better. My only humble request to the community is that more people should come forward and volunteer, especially during times when help is needed. A masjid is not only a place to pray, it is a community center that needs everyone's support and participation.
May Allah reward Imam Saab Dr. Atiq Patel, the management, volunteers, and everyone who contributes to this masjid. May Allah put barakah in their efforts and continue to make Islamic Center of West Georgia a source of guidance, unity, and goodness for the whole community. Ameen.

Whether it is through his leadership, his wisdom, or his constant support for local families, Doctor Sahab’s impact is felt by everyone who walks through these doors. reviews.name: Elizabeth Silver
reviews.text:
I reached out to this masjid sincerely seeking guidance and a better understanding of Islam as someone who is not Muslim. Unfortunately, the response I received left me feeling judged rather than supported. Instead of feeling welcomed into a conversation about faith and learning, I felt assumptions were made and compassion was lacking.

After this experience, I honestly felt very discouraged. Thankfully, another mosque responded with kindness, invited me to learn more, offered guidance, answered my questions, and showed me the compassion and hospitality I had hoped to find. That experience reminded me that one interaction does not represent an entire faith or community.

However, I hope this masjid reflects on how these interactions can impact people who are sincerely seeking understanding. When someone approaches a religious community with an open heart, the way they are treated can influence whether they feel encouraged to continue learning or whether they walk away. Compassion, patience, and humility are powerful ways to represent the values a faith teaches.

reviews.name: Taylor Nur
reviews.text:
Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. As an African American Muslim, I was genuinely excited to find a masjid with a diverse community. I attended for several months, hoping to make it my main masjid.Unfortunately, my experience left me disappointed.
One of my biggest concerns was the conduct of one imam during Jummah. On one occasion, he remarked, "You brothers can't turn to see them, but I can, and they look real nice today." I found this inappropriate for a khutbah and inconsistent with the dignity and modesty that should be upheld from the minbar. I also noticed khutbahs that often seemed unprepared, with rushed recitation and translation of the Qur'an and bashing women. The imam frequently shouted and banged on the minbar which I found distracting rather than beneficial given that they regularly extended to nearly an hour, yet often concluded without a clear central message or takeaway. Then salat would then be led so quickly that it was difficult to pray with composure so many times I had to redo prayer. I was also concerned by the atmosphere within the masjid. Brothers and sisters frequently interacted in ways that, in my understanding of Islam, did not reflect the level of modesty and mindfulness encouraged by our religion. The free mixing is out of control after jummah prayer. Talking during the khutbah and gossip that took away from the sanctity of the masjid. These experiences were deeply upsetting in a place that should feel safe and devoted to the worship of Allah.
Finally, while the masjid regularly announced events and fundraising, I personally did not hear appeals for Muslims facing hardship in places such as Palestine, Sudan,Lebanon, Iran etc. I would love to see more emphasis on support and education of the wider ummah.
I am writing this out of sincere concern, not hatred. I ask Allah (SWT) to bless this community, guide us all to what pleases Him, unite our hearts upon the Qur'an and Sunnah, and accept our efforts. Ameen.

first and foremost May Allah bless this community for trying to hold fast to sunnah of Rasulullah pbuh and for keep stern away from innovations and reminding the people of Tawheed. that is something that is extremely honored by me as a muslimah and i appreciate the sisterhood that i have here unlike any other community.  which is beautiful.  may Allah bless both imams for their efforts to keeping this ummah aright with regular islamic classes and lessons.  very good. also may Allah evevate help and grant them success in this life and the next. imam Khalif Abdisamad has been an imam here for over 20+ years i remember him when i was just a little coming the masjid even when they were at the other location near the somali plaza and halal pizza near the wells fargo.

Seems to me that the woman aren't really heard like i would like them to be in the community. i am a victim of it. which is really sad because we are one ummah but i feel soo left out, unseen and completely feel like as a woman i am of little concern in the community.  i feel treated of little importance when it comes to concerns or advice. the adaab of some of the encounters with a few brothers i came into paths with just made me feel like i am small and puny it's just a feeling i get from certain brothers not all. no one is perfect but it has always bothered me why some of the men act like that, its a certain type of way about them idk but it sometimes make me feel embarrassed to even be a woman just that feeling idk. Again not every brother behaves like this but may Allah guide us all and forgive us Ameen. my voice seems of something as little importance or as no big deal and it hurts and is unfair. it seems as though the men always have a say over the women even if the men are wrong, and we have little support when seeking for aid in regards to unjust men ex. husbands and the like. (Alhumdulilaah the imam helps when he can and may Allah reward him for his efforts Ameen.)it makes me feel helpless as a muslimah and it is definitely a test of faith, but i have no doubt that masjid tawheed is upon The sound creed, and that can never be bartered. i just pray Allah guides us all in this deen and help all of us where we are week and strengthen us as one ummah upon sound aqeedah and good righteous deed and actions. Alhumdulilaah Allah is The bestower of Grace and mercy. May Allah help us all in this ummah and grant us beneficial knowledge and understanding and having beautiful adhab character Ameen. 🌱

afterall this is my OWN personal opinion it may be different for other sisters that attend, but this is something i noticed.  May Allah forgive us all and unite us all upon what is pleasing to him, and may Allah strengthen this community upon goodness in all aspects Ameen. Alhumdulilaah other than that this is a very good community to gain nearness to Allah upon the haqq. May Allah guide us all and protect us, and strengthen us, and bless us all to follow the Qur'an and sunnah of the Phophet Muhammad SALULAAHU ALAHI WAS SALAAM Ameen. MASHA'ALLAH TA'BARAKULLAH

if i said anything wrong May Allah forgive  me. and if i offended anyone it was not my intention.

reviews.text:
This place has become a very special place for me. From the moment you walk in, you feel peace and a sense of belonging. Praying here feels spiritually uplifting. It is a wonderful place for regular salah and Jumu’ah prayer. During Ramadan, the Taraweeh prayers create a deeply emotional and peaceful atmosphere. Peaceful environment for dua, recite the Qur’an, engage in dhikr, and other religious activities. In the last ten nights, many people stay for Qiyam-ul-Layl, which makes the experience even more powerful.

The community here is incredibly warm and welcoming. Every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, they arrange free iftar during Ramadan with many kinds of halal food, drinks, and delicious dishes. What makes it even more beautiful is the kindness of the volunteers. Everyone is very cordial, caring, and always ready to help.

Personally, spending time in this mosque has brought me comfort and spiritual strength. It is not just a place to pray, but a place where you truly feel community, care, and closeness to Allah.

reviews.name: Arfa Khan
reviews.text:
The Imam clearly seems to enjoy the sound of his own voice. Today’s khutbah felt completely pointless — instead of offering meaningful reminders or quoting from authentic hadith, he spent most of the time talking about things like the “Satanic church” and how ChatGPT is supposedly destroying families. It would have been far more beneficial and relevant if he had focused on Islamic teachings supported by Qur’an and hadith rather than using modern technology as an exaggerated example.

The khutbah began at 1:50 PM and didn’t end until 3:00 PM, yet the salah itself lasted less than a minute. According to hadith, the Prophet ﷺ advised that the khutbah should be short and concise, ideally proportionate to the length of the prayer — not the other way around.

Ironically, the Imam spoke about the virtue of praying Fajr in congregation, yet this very community center isn’t even open during Fajr time. It’s disheartening to see such hypocrisy from those who preach one thing but fail to uphold it in practice.

This place is being run by individuals who seem disconnected from the true spirit of Islam. They need to revisit the proper rulings and etiquette of Jumu’ah, and remember that the goal of a khutbah is to inspire faith and reflection, not to deliver long-winded speeches filled with irrelevant topics and contradictions.

reviews.text:
Darul Quran Academy & Masjid has truly become a blessing for our family. My son loves his summer camp and school here, and I'm grateful for how the teachers and staff pour into these children with patience, discipline, and real Islamic character. The environment is clean, structured, and rooted in Qur'an and Sunnah, and you can feel the sincerity as soon as you walk in.

And the sisters -- they are amazing. Supportive, welcoming, and always ready to help. Their kindness and unity make this masjid feel like a second home. May Allah reward everyone who serves this community and continues to build a place where our children can grow in knowledge, faith, and confidence.

The imam at Darul Quran Academy & Masjid is a true example of someone who follows the teachings of the Prophet ﷺ with sincerity and consistency. You can see it in the way he carries himself — calm, patient, and rooted in authentic Sunnah. His reminders are clear, his leadership is balanced, and he treats the community with the same gentleness and wisdom our Prophet taught.

He doesn’t just teach Islam; he lives it. The way he guides the youth, supports the families, and maintains the masjid shows a heart dedicated to serving Allah and uplifting the ummah. May Allah reward him for being a leader who reflects the character, mercy, and guidance of Rasulullah ﷺ.

reviews.name: Lena
reviews.text: The sunnah followed here is great. I was here for the first time this Ramadan and few things i was told by few ladies there that the ladies don’t follow the proper hygiene protocols when preparing food like washing dates or fruits or wear gloves when putting food in plates. Also the Imam reads so fast that he tends to forget a lot. An advice for him is to slow down in his qirat so there is more reward for him and others. A great thing i witnessed was the teacher that was teaching the little young girls i can’t recall her name but she is very dedicated and the students seem to love her. After taraveeh she distributed the young girls gifts and stickers for praying. I may stop by on occasion but I don’t think I can be a regular here although this is right across from where I live.

reviews.name: Syed Ahmed Owais
reviews.text:
I had a wonderful time at this stunning mosque. Its architecture is absolutely beautiful, creating a serene and welcoming atmosphere. One of the highlights for me was praying Tahajjud alone—it was peaceful and spiritually uplifting. The mosque also offers a surprisingly spacious area where I enjoyed playing table tennis, which added a fun and social touch to the visit.

Don’t miss the quirky detail: the covers on the top LEDs! It’s a small thing, but it shows the thoughtful design throughout the space. Whether you're coming for prayer, reflection, or just to admire the beauty, this mosque is a must-visit

reviews.name: Julie Roddy
reviews.text:
As a new revert I was very nervous. Unsure of if I’d be welcomed however all my concerns were for nothing. I have never felt more welcome than at Al Nur. The brothers and sisters are very friendly and supportive of my journey in Islam.

The masjid is a very cozy atmosphere. It allows for the intimacy of family. It is always clean as a few brothers handle it regularly.

They have Quarnic Arabic classes alongside taalim from 1:30pm-6pm on Sundays. It’s very educational it is helping me to understand how to read the Qur’an not in Urdu nothing wrong with reading it in Urdu however it is good to be knowledgeable and understanding of the Qur’an in all ways.

Jumu’ah is from 1:30pm to around 3pm.

There is advanced classes for the Qur’an hosted by Imam Yahya Wednesday and Friday Nights from 8pm until 10:30-11pm.

There is separate restrooms and entrances for the sisters and brothers. With an area to do Wudu and if needed ghusl. There are extra hijabs for the sisters or even just curious ladies. Overall Al Nur is a great place to worship Allah and give him praises. It feels like a second home.

reviews.name: love lift
reviews.text: It's pretty and clean inside! :) The people are nice, too. The Muslim community in Macon is very, very small compared to the large metro-Atlanta area. It seems to be run by a small handful of people. I don't think that they have the resources to maintain their website and keep someone 24/7 at the location (or on the phone services). It's best to go there in person around the timings of prayer, especially Friday prayers. It gets packed then :)

reviews.name: Rashad Ibn
reviews.text: Excellent Masjid, I have attended several times, they are welcoming to all people, and have been supported by Churches in the area after vandalism has taken place. After reading some of the comments I would say to those who read the Quran, or this community and only see bad, please be open. Given our often biased, polluted perceptions and lives, it may be your Creator reading you... In Quran God the Creator invites all of Humanity to be One and at Peace. Good begets good, and evil begets evil. Lets get busy doing the good. God Bless
